audit.whatIsWrong: Every single row of the level chart renders two opposite answers: full phases[0..6].side all read "Fizz" at 7-8/10, while content win[0..6] all read "Aurora". Seven contradictions on one matchup.
audit.why: The full layer is the coherent half — it matches diff HARD, 8/10 difficulty, 8.5/10 carry threat and a 48.17% win rate over 1422 games. An all-Aurora chart cannot be right on a lane Aurora loses. But all-Fizz is not right either: he is melee with no ranged ability whatsoever until Playful / Trickster at 3, so a 900-range Q at levels 1-2 is damage he has no answer to. The kit gives a clean split — Aurora owns 1 and 2, Fizz owns 3 onward once the untargetable hop exists.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-1 flipped to Aurora on both layers (phases side + win + rating), rows 2-6 flipped to Fizz on the content layer to match the full layer. All seven phases[N].why and all seven whys[N] rewritten in the same proposal to argue the side they now sit under.
sources: fizz kit Q range 550 / E range 400 and 16s cooldown

audit.whatIsWrong: The most important interaction is stated BACKWARDS in three places. whys[5], spikes[3].text and late all say Between Worlds "phases through his untargetable dodge tool" and lets you land the combo anyway. Riot's R text gives Aurora a leap, a shockwave, a slowing zone and a cross-zone teleport — no way to hit an untargetable unit. It is his E that beats her burst, not her R that beats his E. Separately, whys[3], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1] all say to dash through or sidestep Chum the Waters with E — but the fish attaches to any champion that touches it, so the dodge has to happen before contact, and Aurora's E hops backward rather than dashing through anything.
audit.why: Getting this inverted teaches the reader to commit into the one window where their damage cannot land, and to try to shake off a projectile that is already attached.
audit.corrected: Untargetability re-stated as his advantage — bait it, then burst the landing. Chum the Waters re-stated as attach-on-touch, dodged before contact only.
sources: aurora kit R and E text

audit.whatIsWrong: Fizz's passive was never mentioned once across either layer, and breakdown.spikes said "Luden's makes the rotation half a bar" while phases[3].why claimed "three-spell spirit stacks proc your passive haste".
audit.why: Nimble Fighter takes a flat amount of reduced damage from ALL sources — which is precisely why a poke-and-chip plan underperforms here, and it explains a 48.17% win rate better than anything else on the page. Aurora's passive heals and grants no haste. "Half a bar" has no source.
audit.corrected: Nimble Fighter now named in tldr, early, spikes[2], report[5] and phases[5].why; spike text rebuilt on his real timings (3 for the hop, 6 for the fish).

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all, and mid called Chum the Waters "a long cooldown" without ever giving it.
audit.why: Playful / Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8 — the number that defines the lane, since it halves across the game. Urchin Strike is 8s at 550, Seastone Trident is 7s down to 3s, Chum the Waters is 120/100/80 at 1300 range.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, winCon, loading, mid, late and the phase whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seastone Trident is described as a thrown poke spell — "his short trident throw" (early), "his short-range trident poke" (wants.you[0]), "Fizz's Seastone Trident poke is short range" (spikes[0]).
audit.why: Riot's W text: his attacks bleed enemies, and he can empower his NEXT ATTACK. It is an auto-attack empower, not a thrown ability. Fizz has no ranged poke at all — which is a much stronger point in Aurora's favour early than the one the page was making, and the brief flags the auto-reset wind-up as the real burst tell.
audit.corrected: Corrected everywhere; early now states outright that he has no ranged poke and that everything starts with Urchin Strike closing 550.

audit.whatIsWrong: early claimed "the third-hit Trickster hop — it resets his jump timer".
audit.why: Nothing in Riot's E text mentions a third-hit reset. Playful / Trickster is one cast with an optional second hop before the slam; there is no reset condition anywhere in the ability.
audit.corrected: Removed. The genuine unstated mechanic — the passive letting him walk through the minion line — is used instead, in dontsFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr said "his dive ignores the knockback", and report[10].t said "Your E knockback-slow is clean gank setup".
audit.why: Aurora's E has no knockback — Riot's text is damage and slow, then a backward hop. Two fields invented a knockback and then built advice on top of it.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around what E actually does.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood pasted, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad pasted, dosFull[0].d was breakdown.cooldowns pasted, and dosFull[2].d described a whiffed E under the title "Crash waves and ping his roams".
audit.corrected: Each body rewritten against its own title.

edits.before: Fizz needs to get in trident range to do anything, and Playful/Trickster has a real cooldown you can track, so if you poke him with Q from range and dash away with E the moment he jumps, you deny his entire early kit. He has zero ranged poke outside his short trident throw, so respecting his engage range while chipping him down wins the lane cleanly. Watch for the third-hit Trickster hop — it resets his jump timer, so don't assume he's fully committed after the first one.
edits.after: Fizz has no ranged poke — Seastone Trident empowers his attacks rather than throwing anything — so everything starts with Urchin Strike closing 550 onto a target. Hold Q at 900 and he has to spend that dash to be in the fight at all. Two things blunt the obvious answer: Nimble Fighter cuts a flat amount from every source of damage, so chip is worth less here than it looks, and Playful / Trickster makes him untargetable for the whole hop. Trade in full patterns, on the landing, never into the air.

edits.before: At level 6 Chum the Waters becomes his real threat: a hit knocks you up into a full burst combo, but the fish travels slowly enough that E's dash lets you sidestep it if you're watching for the cast. Once you've dodged one fish, he's out a long cooldown and forced back into short-range trident pokes you already outclass. Keep shoving waves to deny his ability to freely hop around for extra poke angles.
edits.after: Level 6 is where the lane stops being yours. Chum the Waters is thrown from 1300 and attaches to the first champion it touches, so the moment of counterplay is the throw, not the arrival — after it sticks, the shark erupts, knocks you up, and nothing in your kit takes it off. Dodging one does cost him 120 seconds at rank 1, and that gap is your window. Until then, stand where the fish has to travel a long way to reach you.

edits.before: Your damage race stays ahead of his all-in burst even through his Riftmaker/Lich Bane spike, since your ranged poke chips him before he can safely dive with Trickster. edits.after: Late, what decides it is in his kit, not yours. Playful / Trickster is 8 seconds at rank 5 and untargetable, so your burst has to be spent on a landing rather than on a cast. And Chum the Waters knocks nearby enemies aside as well as knocking up its target, so a grouped fight is the one he is looking for — spread, and make him pick one.

notes: CHART: this matchup shipped with all seven rows contradicting themselves — full sides all "Fizz", content win[] all "Aurora". I resolved rather than left it, because a seven-row disagreement is the exact failure the brief describes and because the win rate (48.17% over 1422 games) plus HARD 8/10 settles the direction. The split I wrote — Aurora rows 1-2, Fizz rows 3 onward — is grounded on Fizz having literally no ranged ability until Playful / Trickster at level 3. If the user prefers the full layer's original all-Fizz reading, only rows 0 and 1 need reverting and the whys I wrote for them would need to flip with them. FLAGS THAT CONTRADICT RIOT'S TEXT, NOT USED: Fizz's E carries derived flags for grounding and slow, and his R carries revealsStealth — none of those appear in Riot's descriptions of those abilities, so per the brief I trusted the description and wrote none of them. If Playful / Trickster does ground, that matters enormously here (it would switch off Aurora's W and R), so it is worth a real source. UNVERIFIED AND NOT WRITTEN: whether Aurora's W invisibility drops Chum the Waters' attachment or breaks its tracking; whether anything at all removes the fish once attached; whether Fizz's E untargetability eats an in-flight Aurora Q curse or only blocks new casts; and whether tenacity shortens the shark knock-up. ITEM NAMES: content spikes referenced Riftmaker/Lich Bane on Fizz and Liandry's/Nashor's on Aurora while the full layer says Luden's — I removed the item claims I rewrote rather than pick a build, since I cannot verify 26.15 itemisation from the kits.
